title: A finite affine cover bounds quasi-coherent cohomology on an open of an affine scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U\subseteq Y$ be an open subscheme, and let $s\ge0$ be an integer. Suppose $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^{s}U_i$ with every $U_i$ affine. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every integer $p\ge s$, one has $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$, where $H^p(U,-)=R^p\Gamma(U,-)$ is module-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. The empty cover $s=0$, and thus $U=\varnothing$, is allowed. No field, Noetherian, finite-type or minimal-cover hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01XI, lemma-vanishing-nr-affines, specialized to an open subscheme of an affine scheme; a cover with s members gives t(U) <= s. For s=0 use the zero module category on the empty scheme.

proof.text: For $s=0$ the covering equality forces $U=\varnothing$. A sheaf of abelian groups has exactly one section over the empty open, by the sheaf axiom for the empty covering. Consequently every module sheaf on $U$ has zero global sections, as does every term of any injective resolution. The section complex is therefore the zero complex, whose kernel modulo image in every degree is zero. By the definition of module cohomology this proves $H^p(U,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $p\ge0$, including $p=0$.

source.place: Tag 01DZ, section-cohomology-sheaves; elementary empty-space case supplementing Tag 01XI

proof.text: Choose an affine presentation $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$. The resulting isomorphism $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated: the projection $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}Y\to Y$ has the diagonal as its inverse, so the diagonal is an isomorphism; an isomorphism is a homeomorphism onto the whole (closed) target with an isomorphism, hence a surjection, on structure sheaves. Thus it is a closed immersion by definition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] to $f$. Every pair of affine opens of $Y$ has affine intersection. Every affine open of $U$ is also an affine open of $Y$, since the composite of the two open inclusions identifies it with the same open subscheme of $Y$. This supplies the intersection assertion for all affine opens used below, without any field hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01KP, lemma-characterize-separated (1)(a), applied to an affine presentation of Y

proof.text: For every open inclusion $j:W\hookrightarrow U$, the pullback formula identifies $j^*\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F|_W$: the inverse image along an open inclusion is restriction, $j^{-1}\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_W$, and $\mathcal O_W\otimes_{\mathcal O_W}(-)$ is the identity. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] this restricted module is quasi-coherent. Use [lem-pc-open-restriction-module-cohomology] whenever comparing the ambient derived evaluation $R^p\Gamma_W(\mathcal F)$ with the module cohomology $H^p(W,\mathcal F|_W)$ on the open scheme. Its natural isomorphism after forgetting scalar actions suffices for vanishing. Thus the affine-vanishing and Mayer--Vietoris statements below use precisely the cohomology of the item, not an unproved identification with Ext of an underlying abelian sheaf.

Prove the assertion by strong induction on the given cover size $s$, simultaneously for all opens of an affine scheme and all quasi-coherent modules on them. The case $s=0$ is step 1. If $s=1$, then $U=U_1$ is affine and $p\ge1$, so [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing], with ambient scheme $U$, gives the assertion. Now let $s\ge2$ and assume the assertion for smaller cover sizes. Put $V=\bigcup_{i=1}^{s-1}U_i$ and $W=U_s$. The opens $V,W$ cover $U$, and $V\cap W=\bigcup_{i=1}^{s-1}(U_i\cap W)$. Step 2 makes each member of this latter cover affine. Apply the induction hypothesis at size $s-1$ to the opens $V$ and $V\cap W$ of the same affine scheme $Y$, with the quasi-coherent restrictions from step 3. For $p\ge s$ it gives $H^p(V,\mathcal F|_V)=0$ and $H^{p-1}(V\cap W,\mathcal F|_{V\cap W})=0$, since $p-1\ge s-1$. The affine vanishing lemma also gives $H^p(W,\mathcal F|_W)=0$, since $p>0$.

Apply [lem-sc-mayer-vietoris-ringed-space] to the ringed space $U$, its two-open cover $V\cup W$, and the $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$. The segment in degree $p$ is exact:
$$H^{p-1}(V\cap W,\mathcal F|_{V\cap W})\longrightarrow H^p(U,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^p(V,\mathcal F|_V)\oplus H^p(W,\mathcal F|_W).$$
The outer groups vanish by step 4, with the open/global identifications of step 3. For any element $x$ of the middle group its image on the right is zero, so exactness writes $x$ as the image of an element of the zero group on the left; hence $x=0$. This completes the induction for the supplied cover size. No minimality of the cover or nonemptiness of its members was used.
